title: First Trimester Nutrition Checklist: Folate, Iron, and Safer Foods
excerpt: Prioritize folic acid, iron-rich foods, hydration, and cooked foods during weeks 1–12
content:
## Introduction to First Trimester Nutrition

During the first trimester, nutrition plays a crucial role in fetal development. Providing adequate nutrients helps prevent birth defects and ensures the health of both mother and baby. In this article, we will explore the essential factors in first trimester nutrition, including folate, iron, and safer foods.

## Folate: A Crucial Nutrient

Folate is a vital vitamin B that helps prevent birth defects such as neural tube defects. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), folate is essential for fetal development. To provide adequate folate, pregnant women should consume folate-rich foods like leafy greens, fruits, and dairy products.

## Iron: An Essential Nutrient

Iron is a vital nutrient that helps prevent anemia and ensures the health of both mother and baby. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), iron is essential for fetal development. To provide adequate iron, pregnant women should consume iron-rich foods like red meat, poultry, and legumes.

## Safer Foods

During the first trimester, pregnant women need to be cautious when choosing foods. According to the National Health Service (NHS), pregnant women should avoid foods like sushi, sashimi, and undercooked meat. Instead, they should opt for cooked foods that are safe and healthy.

## Cooking Foods Safely

To cook foods safely, pregnant women should follow these steps:

* Wash hands thoroughly before cooking
* Wash all ingredients before cooking
* Cook foods to a safe temperature
* Avoid leaving foods at room temperature for too long

## Conclusion

First trimester nutrition is crucial for fetal development. Pregnant women should prioritize providing adequate folate, iron, and safer foods to ensure the health of both mother and baby. For more information on prenatal nutrition, pregnant women can visit [our website](/blog) or [sign up for premium](/premium) to receive guidance from nutrition experts.

## When to Seek Help

If pregnant women have any questions or concerns about nutrition during the first trimester, they should seek help from healthcare professionals. They can also visit [our website](/blog/topics) for more information on prenatal nutrition and related topics.
